topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing complement, noting its complexity, and setting expectations for the session.

topics.label: Fundamentals of complement and component C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of complement, including its general organization, nomenclature rules, and the central role of component C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three activation pathways that converge on deposited C3 to achieve the critical threshold required for complement cascade initiation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream effector functions through which activated complement eradicates pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement from attacking and damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct disease presentations and clinical vulnerabilities caused by deficiencies in individual complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the diverse strategies that pathogens utilize to evade complement-mediated immune destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and preview of next session
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
